title: Tiered batching observability dashboards — mockup (draft slides)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Tiered batching observability dashboards (mockup)
Draft for review
Owners: Observability (Allison), SRE (Aisha/Sergio)
Last updated: 2025-03-18

Speaker notes:
- This deck is the “what we want to see” before we finalize panel JSON + alert rules.
- Goal: dashboards that let on-call answer “is this tier behaving?” + “why did p95 move?” within ~5 minutes.


Slide 2 — Why dashboards / what we’re trying to prevent
Problems we’ve seen in perf canaries + early beta:
- Tail latency regressions from queue delay overshoot (p95/p99 jumps)
- Streaming cadence regressions (tokens stall even when p95 is OK)
- Overload protection interaction (load shed spikes, timeouts climb)
- Silent cost regression (util drops; $/1M tokens goes up)

Success criteria for observability:
- Tier adherence visible per model/region/route
- Clear drill-down from “latency bad” → “queue delay vs prefill vs decode vs overload vs cancellations”
- Rollout monitoring panels built-in (flag % / cohort)

Speaker notes:
- We’re optimizing for operational clarity, not just pretty graphs.
- Also: customers will ask “did fast tier actually run?” → we need effective tier labels everywhere.


Slide 3 — Scope + audience
Audience:
- SRE on-call (hosted + dedicated)
- Runtime on-call / performance triage
- Product/Optimize during beta ramp
- Support/Solutions Engineering (read-only)

In scope for v1:
- Per-tier latency and SLO tracking
- Queue delay + batch formation KPIs
- GPU utilization + throughput
- Errors/timeouts/cancels + overload events
- Streaming token cadence checks

Out of scope for v1:
- Per-customer bespoke auto-tuning visualizations (beyond tier)
- Deep kernel profiling (Nsight) links (can be added later)

Speaker notes:
- We can iterate; v1 must work for rollout go/no-go.


Slide 4 — Glossary / dimensions (consistent naming)
Key dimensions (filters):
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- region
- model_id (or model family)
- gpu_sku
- route: chat | completions | embeddings | rerank
- streaming: true | false
- batching_tier: fast | standard | cost_efficient
- effective_batching_tier: (after precedence rules)
- workload_bucket: prompt_len_bucket, concurrency_bucket (from scheduler signals)

Core derived KPIs:
- SLO latency: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end
- Queue delay: time_in_queue_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- Batch formation: formed_batch_size, batch_wait_ms, batch_fill_ratio
- Util: sm_util, mem_util, kv_cache_util, tokens/s, req/s

Speaker notes:
- “effective_batching_tier” must exist to avoid confusion when customers set explicit overrides.
- We’ll standardize on tier labels from slo-toolkit helper (ref PR 267).


Slide 5 — Dashboard layout (top-level navigation)
Proposed folder: “Tiered batching (SLO tiers)” with 4 dashboards:
1) Overview — Tier health (executive view)
2) Latency deep-dive — E2E + stage breakdown
3) Batch/Queue mechanics — formation + queue delay + scheduling
4) Rollout & Alerts — canary, flag ramps, guardrails

Common UX elements:
- Left-side variables: env, deployment_mode, region, model_id, route, streaming, gpu_sku, effective_batching_tier
- “Compare tiers” toggle: show fast vs standard vs cost_efficient overlays (same model/region)

Speaker notes:
- We’ve had issues where dashboards are too fragmented; folder approach keeps it discoverable.
- “Compare tiers” is key during tuning. Implementation can be Grafana repeat panels or multi-series.


Slide 6 — Dashboard 1: Overview — Tier health (top row)
Panels (row 1):
- E2E latency p95 by tier (overlay)
- E2E latency p99 by tier (overlay)
- Error rate (%) + timeout rate (%) by tier
- Tokens/sec and req/sec by tier

Row 2:
- Queue delay p95 by tier
- Mean formed_batch_size + p95 formed_batch_size
- GPU SM util (%) + GPU mem util (%)
- KV cache pressure: kv_cache_util p95 + OOM/preempt counters

Row 3 (rollout awareness):
- Feature flag enablement % (by region/model) vs time
- “Cohort size” (requests) by tier (so we know if data is meaningful)

Speaker notes:
- This is the “NOC wall” view.
- If only 2% traffic is on cost_efficient, we should annotate that before overreacting to noise.


Slide 7 — Dashboard 1: Overview — annotations + SLO overlays
Add SLO target bands per tier:
- fast: target p95 band (ms) + p99 band (ms)
- standard: target bands
- cost_efficient: target bands

Annotations:
- Runtime deploy (version)
- Flag ramp changes (percentage adjustments)
- Config changes (tier defaults updated in model registry)

Speaker notes:
- SLO numbers come from SRE doc “latency-slo-tiers-fast-standard-costefficient”.
- Annotating deploys + flag ramps is non-negotiable; otherwise everyone correlates wrong.


Slide 8 — Dashboard 2: Latency deep-dive (what’s making p95 move?)
Panels:
- E2E latency: p50/p95/p99 (3 graphs) split by stage:
  - queue_delay_ms
  - prefill_ms
  - decode_ms (or “generation_ms”)
  - postproc_ms (tooling/serialization)
- First-token latency (streaming=true) p95/p99
- Time-to-last-token (streaming=true) p95/p99
- Token cadence: tokens_per_second p50/p95 (streaming=true)

Drilldown table:
- Top (model_id, region, gpu_sku) by “p95 delta vs baseline” with links to Batch/Queue dashboard

Speaker notes:
- The stage breakdown is the only way to separate “we queued too long” vs “decode got slower” vs “prefill got slower due to long prompts”.
- For streaming, we need separate first-token and cadence; otherwise regressions hide.


Slide 9 — Dashboard 2: Latency deep-dive (distribution + outliers)
Panels:
- Heatmap: queue_delay_ms distribution over time (per tier)
- Heatmap: formed_batch_size distribution over time (per tier)
- Scatter: queue_delay_ms vs formed_batch_size (sampled traces) colored by workload_bucket
- Tail focus: 99.5th / 99.9th percentile (where supported) to catch “rare spikes”

Speaker notes:
- During beta we saw rare queue delay spikes that don’t move p99 much until traffic increases.
- Scatter plot can be approximated with exemplars/traces if Grafana can’t do true scatter reliably.


Slide 10 — Dashboard 3: Batch/Queue mechanics (are we batching “as intended”?)
Panels:
- Batch formation rate: batches_formed/sec
- Mean formed_batch_size + p95 formed_batch_size (by tier)
- batch_wait_ms p50/p95 (time spent waiting to fill)
- batch_fill_ratio (formed_batch_size / max_batch_size) p50/p95
- Admission control events:
  - rejected_requests/sec (by reason)
  - queued_requests gauge

Tier knobs visibility (informational):
- max_batch_size (effective)
- max_queue_delay_ms (effective)
- prefill/decode scheduling weights (effective)

Speaker notes:
- We should show the “effective knob values” (from config explain endpoint) next to the mechanics so people can sanity-check quickly.
- This is where “tier selection didn’t apply” becomes obvious.


Slide 11 — Dashboard 3: KV cache + memory pressure (cost_efficient risk area)
Panels:
- kv_cache_util (%) p50/p95
- kv_cache_evictions/sec + kv_cache_compactions/sec
- GPU mem util (%) p50/p95
- OOM events count (with model_id/gpu_sku)
- Prefill length: prompt_tokens distribution (to detect long-context traffic)

Guardrail indicators:
- “KV pressure limit triggered” counter
- “Decode deprioritized due to pressure” counter (if available)

Speaker notes:
- Most cost_efficient failures look like memory pressure → fallback → timeouts.
- Even if we don’t have all counters day 1, reserve layout so we can add them without re-training everyone.


Slide 12 — Dashboard 4: Rollout & Alerts (canary control panel)
Panels:
- Traffic split: % requests by effective_batching_tier (per model/region)
- Error budget burn rate (per tier) — 1h and 6h windows
- Auto-rollback status (enabled/triggered) and last trigger reason
- “Go/No-Go checklist” mini table (see next slide)

Alert groups (preview):
- Latency SLO breach (p95/p99)
- Queue delay inflation
- Streaming cadence regression
- Timeout/cancel spike
- Load shed spike

Speaker notes:
- This is intended to be used live during ramp (feature flag percentage increases).
- We want a single page that answers “are we safe to proceed from 10% → 25%?”


Slide 13 — Rollout monitoring checklist (embedded in dashboard as table)
Checklist items (green/yellow/red):
1) fast tier: p95 within target band and stable (last 30m)
2) standard tier: p95 within target band and stable (last 30m)
3) cost_efficient tier: error rate not elevated vs standard (relative threshold)
4) queue_delay p95 not increased > X ms vs baseline for streaming routes
5) tokens/sec not decreased > Y% (proxy for throughput regression)
6) load_shed events not increased > Z% (overload interaction)
7) OOM events == 0 for cohort (or below tolerated tiny baseline)

Speaker notes:
- We’ll wire this as a computed table later; for now it’s a layout proposal.
- Exact X/Y/Z thresholds are to be finalized with SRE (Sean/Rafael) based on perf canary + beta data.


Slide 14 — Alert thresholds (proposal, not final)
Notes:
- Alerts should be tier-aware and route-aware (streaming is special).
- We should prefer “relative regression vs baseline” for early beta to avoid hardcoding unstable absolute numbers per model.

Candidate rules (initial):
- Page: p95 latency > tier_target_p95 for 10m AND request_rate > min_traffic
- Page: timeout_rate increases by > 2x vs trailing 24h baseline for 10m
- Ticket: queue_delay_p95 increases by > 20ms (streaming) or > 50ms (non-streaming) for 20m
- Ticket: token_cadence_p95 drops by > 15% for 20m (streaming)
- Page: load_shed_rate > 0.5% for 5m (cohort limited)

Speaker notes:
- These are placeholders; we need to avoid noisy alerts from queue-delay (see prior SRE thread). Add min traffic + multi-window.
- Also: ensure alerts are grouped by (model_id, region, effective_batching_tier) so on-call can action.


Slide 15 — Debug flow (how an on-call uses this)
If p95 latency breached:
1) Overview → confirm which tier/model/region
2) Latency deep-dive → determine stage driving (queue vs prefill vs decode)
3) If queue-driven → Batch/Queue mechanics dashboard
   - check queue_delay, batch_wait, formed_batch_size
   - check effective knob values (max_queue_delay_ms)
4) If decode/cadence regression → streaming panels + recent runtime deploy annotation
5) If error/timeouts → Rollout & Alerts
   - check load shed / admission control / OOMs
6) Mitigation options (informational):
   - pause ramp (flag)
   - rollback defaults for affected model/gpu_sku
   - force standard tier for streaming routes

Speaker notes:
- This is the “5-minute triage” path.
- We should link directly between dashboards using Grafana drilldowns with variables carried over.


Slide 16 — Instrumentation dependencies / assumptions
We assume the following metrics exist (names TBD; conceptual list):
- request_latency_ms{stage=e2e|queue|prefill|decode|postproc, route, model_id, region, gpu_sku, effective_batching_tier, streaming}
- queue_delay_ms histogram
- formed_batch_size histogram
- batch_wait_ms histogram
- batch_fill_ratio gauge/histogram
- admission_control_events_total{reason}
- load_shed_events_total{reason}
- timeout_total, cancel_total
- tokens_generated_total, tokens_per_second (or derived)
- gpu_sm_util, gpu_mem_util
- kv_cache_util, kv_cache_evictions_total, kv_cache_compactions_total
- rollout_flag_state{flag_name, model_id, region} (or annotation feed)

Speaker notes:
- ENG-18422 is the primary dependency for queue/batch metrics.
- We also need the “effective config explain” endpoint wiring so we can show knob values (ref runtime PR 18470).


Slide 17 — Open questions / review asks
Questions for review (please comment inline):
1) Do we want one dashboard per deployment_mode, or one dashboard with variable?
2) For customers: do we expose a subset view in Console, or keep full Grafana internal-only?
3) What are the final SLO target bands per tier per route (streaming vs non-streaming)?
4) Which metrics are “must have” for beta ramp vs “nice to have” for GA?
5) Alert noise: what min traffic thresholds + burn-rate style should we enforce?

Owners / next steps:
- Allison + Caleb: confirm metric label set won’t explode cardinality
- Aisha + Sergio: finalize alert policy + paging rules
- Chloe: map internal dashboard panels to Console-friendly subset
- Logan + Nadia: validate cost panels ($/1M tokens proxy) are consistent with billing

Speaker notes:
- Biggest risk is high-cardinality labels (prompt buckets + concurrency buckets). We may need sampled traces for detailed breakdown.
- Please reply with “blocker / not blocker” on the open questions so we can land the dashboard JSON in observability-pack.
